title: Breast Invasive Carcinoma
summary:
TCGA breast is the most heavily analyzed dataset indexed here: 2,463 articles reference it in their methods or results. Its continuing value is less about novelty than about being the common denominator - a cohort so widely used that a new method which cannot reproduce known findings on it is not yet credible.
Two things about it are less widely appreciated. First, its radiology and pathology imaging lives in the Imaging Data Commons rather than the GDC, so the same 1,098 patients carry twelve measurement types once the repositories are joined, and most analyses use only the genomic subset. Second, its treatment annotation is better than its reputation: therapeutic agents are recorded for 71% of cases and a treatment outcome for 64%, which supports response questions people generally assume require a trial cohort.
one_liner: 1,098 breast tumors measured twelve ways across GDC and IDC, with treatment outcome on 64% of cases - the most reused dataset in this corpus and still the reference cohort for method development.

useful_for.question: Does a new computational method reproduce established breast cancer molecular subtypes?
useful_for.rationale: Expression, methylation, copy number, microRNA and protein array data on largely the same 1,098 tumors, with subtype assignments established across hundreds of prior papers. This is the standard benchmark, and the density of prior work is the point.
useful_for.statistical_note: Because so many methods have been tuned on this cohort, strong performance here is weak evidence of generalization. Pair it with an external cohort.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Which molecular features are associated with response to specific systemic therapies?
useful_for.rationale: Therapeutic agents are recorded for 71% of cases - cyclophosphamide, tamoxifen, anastrozole, paclitaxel and doxorubicin are the commonest - and a treatment outcome field is populated for 64%. Combined with expression on 1,095 cases this supports agent-stratified response analysis.
useful_for.statistical_note: Treatment was not randomized and is confounded with stage, subtype and era of care. Any agent comparison needs explicit confounding control and should be framed as associative.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Do radiology or pathology image features add prognostic information beyond molecular data?
useful_for.rationale: Imaging for these same patients is held in the Imaging Data Commons and is openly downloadable, while the molecular data sit in the GDC. Joining them gives a multimodal cohort most users never realise is available.
useful_for.statistical_note: Imaging coverage is not complete across the cohort; build the intersection first and check it is not biased by site or era.

useful_for.question: What distinguishes long-term survivors, given a median follow-up of 27.1 months?
useful_for.rationale: Vital status is informative for 99.9% of cases and follow-up time is computable, giving a clean overall survival endpoint on a large cohort.
useful_for.statistical_note: Breast cancer events accrue over a decade or more, and the median patient here is followed under three years, although a minority reach twenty years. Late-recurrence questions are underpowered.

limitations.statement: Median follow-up is 27.1 months across 1,096 of 1,098 cases, though the maximum reaches 282 months. Breast cancer, particularly hormone receptor positive disease, recurs over ten to twenty years, so the median patient is observed through only the early part of the natural history.
limitations.mitigation: Use restricted mean survival time; do not extrapolate beyond observed follow-up.

limitations.statement: Treatment is observational and unrandomised, recorded retrospectively, and reflects standards of care from the late 2000s. Modern regimens including CDK4/6 inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates and immunotherapy are absent.
limitations.mitigation: Frame findings as historical-cohort associations rather than predictive claims.

limitations.statement: 757 of 1,098 patients are recorded as white and 183 as Black or African American, with 95 not reported. Male breast cancer is present only in very small numbers.
affected_analyses: Disparities research beyond the two largest groups
limitations.mitigation: The 183 Black patients support some disparities work but with limited power for subtype-stratified analysis.

limitations.statement: Methylation uses HM450 and HM27 arrays and copy number uses Affymetrix SNP 6.0 - platforms no longer in routine use, which complicates integration with contemporary data.
limitations.mitigation: Use probe-level harmonization and restrict to shared features.
